text:
UN General Assembly resolutions are not a formal source of international law under Article 38(1) of the ICJ Statute; they are ordinarily recommendations, and they bind member states only in the narrow Charter categories of internal organization and the budget. Their weight as evidence of custom turns on normative wording, the size and quality of support, explanations of vote, and consistency with state practice, so near-universal adoption does not make every resolution a codification of existing custom or conclusive proof of it. Particular resolutions can evidence or help crystallize opinio juris, as with the Friendly Relations Declaration, and many others operate only as soft law that may later harden into custom or treaty rules.

CONFIDENCE: 92
